name: Harry Potter
description: An orphaned boy who learns at eleven that he is a wizard and leaves for Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. The dark wizard Voldemort, who killed his parents, hunts him all his life, and the lightning-shaped scar on his forehead is the mark he left.
fact: Daniel Radcliffe played Harry in the films; he was eleven years old when shooting on the first one began.

name: Hermione Granger
description: One of the ablest students at Hogwarts, and born to an ordinary non-magical family of Muggles. Hermione is sharp-witted, devoted to her books and fiercely loyal, and what she knows saves Harry Potter and Ron Weasley from danger again and again.
fact: Emma Watson won the part of Hermione in the films while she was still a schoolgirl.

name: Severus Snape
description: The grim, sharp-tongued Potions master at Hogwarts, whose true feelings towards Harry Potter stay a mystery for years. Behind the coldness lies a complicated life, bound up closely with the story of the boy's parents.
fact: Alan Rickman knew the character's central secret long before the final books appeared — Rowling told him herself.

name: Lord Voldemort
description: The most powerful dark wizard of his age, obsessed with immortality and with ruling the magical world. Most wizards are too afraid to say his name out loud and call him simply the Dark Lord, or He Who Must Not Be Named.
fact: Ralph Fiennes played the part without the tip of his nose — it was removed with computer graphics.

name: Albus Dumbledore
description: Headmaster of Hogwarts and one of the greatest wizards alive, known for his wisdom and a certain eccentricity. He is Harry Potter's mentor and one of the very few people Voldemort genuinely fears.
fact: Richard Harris was the first Dumbledore on screen; after his death the role passed to Michael Gambon.

name: Frodo Baggins
description: A modest hobbit from the Shire who is handed the task of destroying the One Ring. The long, dangerous journey across Middle-earth to the fires of Mount Doom becomes the hardest of trials and changes him for good.
fact: Elijah Wood, who had been acting since early childhood, played Frodo in Peter Jackson's films.

name: Gandalf
description: A powerful wandering wizard who helps the peoples of Middle-earth stand against the darkness. He first turns up in "The Hobbit" as Bilbo Baggins's mysterious guide, and later becomes the spiritual leader of the Fellowship of the Ring.
fact: Tolkien said Gandalf's look came from a postcard showing an old man wandering in the mountains.

name: Gollum
description: A once hobbit-like creature, twisted by long possession of the One Ring, which he calls "my precious". Two natures fight inside him: a wretched, scheming thing and the faint remains of the kinder person he used to be.
fact: Andy Serkis played Gollum in Peter Jackson's films using motion capture.

name: Aragorn
description: A ranger also known as Strider, who turns out to be the rightful heir to the ancient kingdom of Gondor. He leads the Fellowship of the Ring through the perils of Middle-earth and in the end becomes the king who unites Men against the dark.
fact: Viggo Mortensen was cast as Aragorn at almost the last moment, once filming on the trilogy had already started.

name: Legolas
description: A prince of the woodland elves and a superb archer, one of the Fellowship of the Ring. His deadly aim, keen sight and unlikely friendship with the dwarf Gimli, despite the old feud between their peoples, are among the highlights of the story.
fact: Orlando Bloom trained in archery, riding and swordfighting for the part.

name: Darth Vader
description: A mighty warrior of the dark side of the Force, recognisable by his black mask and heavy mechanical breathing. Once a Jedi knight, he went over to the Empire and became one of the most recognisable villains in the history of cinema.
fact: James Earl Jones voiced Darth Vader in the original trilogy, while another actor wore the costume on set.

name: Luke Skywalker
description: A young man from the desert planet Tatooine who discovers his destiny and becomes one of the last of the Jedi knights. His coming of age and his fight against the Empire form the central thread of the original trilogy.
fact: The shot of Luke watching Tatooine's twin suns set is one of the most recognisable images in the whole saga.

name: Yoda
description: One of the oldest and wisest Jedi in the galaxy, who trains young apprentices in the ways of the Force despite standing barely knee-high. His odd word order and short, pointed sayings have become a fixture of world pop culture.
fact: Frank Oz, also known for his work with the Muppets, puppeteered and voiced Yoda in the original films.

name: Han Solo
description: A cocky pilot and smuggler, captain of the Millennium Falcon, who starts out in it purely for the money and grows into a genuine hero of the rebellion against the Empire. His quick tongue made him one of the best-loved characters in the saga.
fact: The part of Han Solo made Harrison Ford a worldwide star before he ever played Indiana Jones.

name: Princess Leia
description: Princess of Alderaan, the planet destroyed by the Empire, and one of the leaders of the Rebel Alliance. Determined and fearless, she combines a diplomat's skill with a readiness to fight for the galaxy's freedom herself.
fact: Carrie Fisher played Leia in the original trilogy and came back to the role almost forty years later in "The Force Awakens".

name: Chewbacca
description: A towering, enormously strong warrior of the Wookiee people, loyal friend and co-pilot to Han Solo aboard the Millennium Falcon. For all his fearsome looks, he is one of the most devoted and good-natured characters in the saga.
fact: Peter Mayhew, who stood well over two metres tall, played Chewbacca in the original trilogy.

name: R2-D2
description: A small astromech droid, the heroes' faithful companion, able to repair starships and to carry the most closely guarded secrets. He speaks only in beeps and whistles, yet almost everyone around him understands him perfectly.
fact: In some scenes of the original trilogy the short-statured actor Kenny Baker sat inside the R2-D2 shell.

name: Grogu
description: A mysterious infant of the same unnamed species as Master Yoda, born with a strong connection to the Force. A Mandalorian bounty hunter finds him and takes him under his protection, and their touching bond became the heart of the show.
fact: Before his name was revealed, fans around the world simply called him Baby Yoda.

name: Spider-Man
description: Peter Parker, an ordinary high-school student who gains superhuman strength, agility and a sense for danger from the bite of a radioactive spider. He fights crime in New York while staying an unassuming kid in his everyday life.
fact: Stan Lee and Steve Ditko wanted their hero to have the most ordinary teenage problems, unlike most of the heroes around him.

name: Iron Man
description: Billionaire inventor Tony Stark builds a powerful suit of armour to fight evil and to atone for his own weapons falling into the wrong hands. His wit and engineering genius made him one of the most recognisable superheroes anywhere.
fact: Playing Tony Stark in the Marvel Cinematic Universe made Robert Downey Jr. one of the highest-paid actors in the world.

name: Captain America
description: Frail young Steve Rogers, turned by an experimental serum into a super-soldier and a symbol of the fight against fascism in the Second World War. In the present day he remains the standard of soldierly honour among Marvel's heroes.
fact: Captain America was created before the United States entered the Second World War and was fighting Nazis from his very first issue.

name: Thor
description: The mighty Asgardian god of thunder, wielder of the enchanted hammer Mjolnir, which only the worthy can lift. Proud and hot-tempered when his story begins, he slowly learns the wisdom and the responsibility of a ruler.
fact: The Marvel character is based on the Norse god Thor, but over the years he has grown a mythology of his own.

name: Hulk
description: Scientist Bruce Banner, who turns under the force of his own rage into an immensely strong green creature, all but immune to ordinary weapons. The struggle between the thinking man and the destructive monster is the core of his story.
fact: In the comics the Hulk was grey at first, but printing trouble changed his colour to green almost immediately.

name: Black Widow
description: Natasha Romanoff, a former Soviet spy and assassin who switches sides to join the superhero team the Avengers. She has no superpowers and relies in a fight on combat skill, cunning and years of intelligence training.
fact: Scarlett Johansson has played Natasha Romanoff in the Marvel Cinematic Universe since "Iron Man 2".

name: Thanos
description: A colossally powerful Titan obsessed with restoring the balance of the universe by radical and brutal means. Armed with artefacts of unimaginable power, he becomes the largest-scale opponent Marvel's heroes have ever faced.
fact: Josh Brolin played Thanos in the Marvel films, though most of what appears on screen was built with computer graphics.

name: Loki
description: Thor's adopted brother and Marvel's version of the Norse god of mischief, forever balanced between villainy and a need to prove his own worth. His unpredictability made him one of the best-loved antiheroes of the film universe.
fact: Tom Hiddleston landed the role of Loki after originally auditioning for Thor.

name: Deadpool
description: Wade Wilson, a mercenary disfigured by experiments that left him with super-fast healing and a peculiar sense of humour. Unlike most superheroes he talks straight to the audience, breaking the fourth wall whenever he feels like it.
fact: Deadpool began as a parody of DC's Deathstroke: the deliberately similar real names, Wade Wilson and Slade Wilson, are the giveaway.

name: Wolverine
description: Logan, a mutant with a healing factor, heightened senses and retractable claws of near-indestructible metal. His short temper and a past full of loss have made him one of the most popular characters in the Marvel universe.
fact: Hugh Jackman played Wolverine for nearly two decades, longer than most actors in any other superhero franchise.

name: Groot
description: A tree-like alien who can say only the words "I am Groot", though those around him understand him perfectly well. For all his limited vocabulary, he is one of the most loyal and moving members of the Guardians of the Galaxy.
fact: Vin Diesel voiced Groot in the Marvel films, delivering the same line over and over with different shades of meaning.

name: Batman
description: Billionaire Bruce Wayne, who became a masked vigilante after a street robber killed his parents. With no superpowers at all, he relies on his intellect, his fighting skill and an arsenal of gadgets to keep crime out of Gotham.
fact: Batman is one of the few iconic superheroes with no supernatural abilities of any kind.

name: Joker
description: A chaotic criminal genius with a chalk-white painted face and a sinister grin, Batman's chief adversary in Gotham. His real origin is left deliberately vague, and he stands for pure anarchy and unpredictability.
fact: Two actors have won Oscars for playing the Joker in different films: Heath Ledger and Joaquin Phoenix.

name: Superman
description: Kal-El, an alien sent to Earth as a baby from the dying planet Krypton, where he gains superhuman strength, flight and near-total invulnerability. Working as a journalist under the name Clark Kent, he defends the world as a symbol of hope.
fact: Superman is considered one of the first superheroes in the modern sense — his comic appeared back in 1938.

name: Wonder Woman
description: Princess Diana of the Amazons, who left her home island of Themyscira to bring justice and compassion to the world of men. She fights with a magic lasso of truth and superhuman strength, and was among the first truly iconic superheroines.
fact: Wonder Woman's creator, William Marston, was also one of the inventors of an early version of the lie detector.

name: Harley Quinn
description: Harleen Quinzel, a psychiatrist at Gotham's asylum who fell for her patient the Joker, became his accomplice and later struck out as an antiheroine of her own. Her eccentricity, acrobatics and black humour made her one of DC's most popular villains.
fact: Harley Quinn did not start in the comics: she first appeared in the animated "Batman" series in the early nineties.

name: Catwoman
description: Selina Kyle, a nimble burglar who works Gotham in a cat mask and lives on the line between crime and her soft spot for Batman. Her relationship with the Dark Knight is a mix of rivalry, flirtation and genuine mutual respect.
fact: Catwoman turned up in the Batman comics almost at the same time as the Joker himself, back in 1940.

name: James Bond
description: The elegant British intelligence agent with the code number 007, who pairs lethal skills with impeccable style and unshakeable calm. His adventures against international villains became the basis of one of the longest-running film series ever made.
fact: Several different actors have played James Bond on screen over the decades, starting with Sean Connery.

name: Indiana Jones
description: A professor of archaeology who spends his time away from lectures chasing ancient artefacts on dangerous expeditions around the world. His trademark hat and whip are among the most recognisable props in adventure cinema.
fact: Harrison Ford played Indiana Jones across decades, without ever handing the part to another actor.

name: Terminator T-800
description: A cyborg sent back from the future, a metal skeleton under living tissue, built to carry out its mission whatever stands in the way. Depending on the film, it appears either as a merciless assassin or as a protector of human beings.
fact: "I'll be back" was never written as a catchphrase — it became the character's calling card only after the film came out.

name: Rocky Balboa
description: A modest club boxer from Philadelphia who is handed an unexpected shot at the world champion. His story of stubbornness, training and self-belief has stood for beating the odds for several generations of viewers.
fact: Sylvester Stallone wrote the Rocky screenplay himself in order to land the lead, though studios wanted to make it with bigger stars.

name: John Rambo
description: A Vietnam veteran whose survival and combat training turns into a brutal confrontation with the authorities of a quiet small town. The character came to stand for the hard fate of soldiers who came home to an indifferent society.
fact: He was born on the page, not on screen: David Morrell's novel "First Blood" came first, and the film with Sylvester Stallone ten years later.

name: John Wick
description: A legendary contract killer who tried to leave the trade after losing his wife and is dragged back into the criminal world. His cold composure, fighting skill and lightning gunfights made the film series a benchmark for modern action.
fact: Keanu Reeves did much of the stunt and firearms work himself, training for several months before the role.

name: Neo
description: Thomas Anderson, a programmer who learns that the familiar world is a computer simulation and is given the chance to free humanity. The choice between the blue pill and the red pill became one of the most recognisable images in cinema.
fact: Keanu Reeves played Neo, and the film's fight choreography was staged by masters of Hong Kong action cinema.

name: Ellen Ripley
description: An officer on a commercial spacecraft, the only one able to stand up to a lethal alien predator. Her cool head and sheer determination made her one of the first genuinely strong heroines in science fiction cinema.
fact: Sigourney Weaver was nominated for an Oscar for playing Ripley in the sequel "Aliens" — a rarity for a science fiction action film.

name: Marty McFly
description: An ordinary high-school kid who is accidentally sent back to his parents' youth in a modified sports car. He has to get the two of them together without derailing history, while his inventor friend works out how to send him home.
fact: The DeLorean became the time machine at the script stage: in an early draft the part was played by an ordinary refrigerator.

name: Forrest Gump
description: A good-natured Alabama man who, despite his limited intellect, ends up an accidental witness to and participant in the great events of twentieth-century American history. His sincerity and his faithful love for Jenny have moved audiences for decades.
fact: The famous line about a box of chocolates was not in the novel — it was written for the film by its screenwriter.

name: Captain Jack Sparrow
description: The flamboyant and permanently tipsy captain of the Black Pearl, who talks his way out of every scrape with cunning, charm and luck. His unsteady walk and unpredictable decisions became the signature of the whole franchise.
fact: Johnny Depp has said he built the character around the manner of the musician Keith Richards.

name: Hannibal Lecter
description: A brilliant psychiatrist of refined intellect and refined taste, whose exquisite manners hide a taste for monstrous crimes. His reluctant cooperation with investigators hunting another killer became the basis of a cult thriller.
fact: The part won Anthony Hopkins an Oscar even though his screen time in the film is remarkably short.

name: Tyler Durden
description: A brash, magnetic soap salesman who sets up an underground fight club as a protest against consumer society. His philosophy of self-destruction and freedom from possessions turns ordinary men into members of a radical movement.
fact: The character first appeared in Chuck Palahniuk's novel, and David Fincher's film adaptation is what made him a cult figure.

name: Vito Corleone
description: The respected and feared head of an Italian-American mafia family, who lives by his own hard code of honour and justice. His quiet authority and famously hoarse voice have been imitated countless times ever since.
fact: The role won Marlon Brando an Oscar, which he then publicly refused to accept.

name: Tony Montana
description: An ambitious Cuban emigrant who climbs to the top of the Miami drug trade by brutal and headlong means. His limitless hunger for power and his famous closing line made him a cult figure of crime cinema.
fact: Al Pacino played Tony Montana and worked specially on the character's Cuban accent.

name: Sherlock Holmes
description: The sharp-eyed London consulting detective who solves the most tangled crimes through deduction and attention to the smallest detail. His friendship with Doctor Watson, his pipe and the deerstalker hat are the very image of the classic detective.
fact: Arthur Conan Doyle tried to kill Holmes off in one of the stories, but readers put him under so much pressure that he brought him back.

name: Doctor Watson
description: A retired army doctor who becomes Sherlock Holmes's flatmate and constant companion on his investigations. Most of the stories are told in his voice, and his practical good sense sets off the eccentric genius of his friend.
fact: The name Doctor Watson has become a byword for the faithful assistant of a brilliant specialist.

name: Hercule Poirot
description: An eccentric Belgian detective with a magnificent moustache, who relies on the "little grey cells" of his mind rather than on brute force. His neatness and love of order untangle the most ingenious crimes in Agatha Christie's novels.
fact: Agatha Christie grew tired of her own creation over the years, once calling him an insufferable and tiresome man.

name: Count Dracula
description: A Transylvanian vampire count who has lived for centuries on human blood and can take the shape of a bat. The figure Bram Stoker created is the source of very nearly all modern vampire mythology in popular culture.
fact: The count is thought to be based in part on the fifteenth-century Wallachian ruler Vlad the Impaler, notorious for his cruelty.

name: Frankenstein's monster
description: The nameless creature assembled by the scientist Victor Frankenstein from parts of dead bodies and brought to life by a means science cannot explain. For all his terrifying looks, in Mary Shelley's novel he is a suffering, lonely being rejected by his own maker.
fact: In popular culture the creator's name, Frankenstein, has long been misapplied to the monster itself.

name: King Kong
description: An enormous intelligent gorilla from the lost Skull Island, captured and shipped to New York as a curiosity. His final climb up a skyscraper became one of the most recognisable images in the history of monster cinema.
fact: In the original 1933 film Kong was brought to life through stop-motion animation of a small model.

name: Godzilla
description: A colossal monster woken by nuclear testing and able to breathe a devastating atomic ray. Conceived as a metaphor for the horrors of nuclear weapons, the creature went on to become one of the most recognisable monsters in world cinema.
fact: The original 1954 Godzilla suit weighed tens of kilograms, and the actor inside could barely move in it.

name: Tarzan
description: An English aristocrat by birth, raised by apes in the African jungle after his parents died. His extraordinary strength, his famous yell and his friendship with the animals made him one of the great heroes of adventure fiction and film.
fact: Tarzan's famous cry in the old films was built in the studio by mixing several different sound recordings together.

name: Zorro
description: A nobleman who puts on a mask and cape to defend the ordinary people of California against the injustice of the colonial authorities. His trademark, a letter Z slashed with a sword, became the emblem of the noble masked avenger.
fact: The character shaped Batman: in comics canon Bruce Wayne lost his parents on the way home from a Zorro film.

name: Robin Hood
description: The legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest who robs the rich and gives to the poor together with his band of merry men. His feud with the cruel Sheriff of Nottingham and his deadly aim with a bow have fed countless books and films.
fact: Historians still argue over whether there was any real person behind the legend.

name: Peter Pan
meta: the boy who never grew up
description: The boy who refused to grow up and lives on the magical island of Neverland among fairies and pirates. He can fly and teaches the Darling children to do the same, and his eternal adversary is the scheming Captain Hook.
fact: His name has become a byword for grown-ups who never quite managed to grow up on the inside.

name: Alice in Wonderland
description: An inquisitive English girl who follows the White Rabbit down his hole and lands in an absurd magical country. Her encounters with the Cheshire Cat, the Mad Hatter and the Queen of Hearts are classics of English nonsense literature.
fact: Lewis Carroll invented the story on a boating trip with a real girl named Alice and her sisters.

name: Winnie-the-Pooh
description: A good-natured stuffed bear of very little brain and an unwavering love of honey, who lives in the Hundred Acre Wood. Together with his friends Piglet, Eeyore and Tigger he lives through small but touching stories about friendship.
fact: The bear was based on a real stuffed toy belonging to the son of the author, A. A. Milne.

name: Karlsson on the Roof
meta: little fat man with a propeller
description: A funny, boastful little fat man who lives on the roof of a Stockholm building and flies with a propeller on his back. He becomes the secret friend of a lonely little boy, drawing him into his pranks and his gloriously absurd schemes.
fact: In Astrid Lindgren's Swedish original he is Karlsson på taket — Karlsson on the roof.

name: Pippi Longstocking
meta: the strongest girl in the world
description: A red-haired girl with sticking-out plaits who lives alone in her own house with a monkey and a horse and no grown-ups at all. With superhuman strength and complete disregard for convention, she turns a quiet Swedish town upside down.
fact: Astrid Lindgren made the story up for her own daughter when she was ill, and the girl chose the heroine's name herself.

name: The Little Prince
description: A mysterious boy who has come from a tiny asteroid where the one rose of his life grows. His meeting with a pilot stranded in the desert turns into a philosophical fable about love, friendship and seeing what really matters.
fact: Saint-Exupéry's book is among the most translated in the world, outdone in the number of languages by very few titles.

name: Pinocchio
description: A wooden puppet carved by the old joiner Geppetto, who longs to become a real live boy. Every lie he tells makes his nose grow longer, and his road to becoming human runs through one instructive disaster after another.
fact: The original Italian tale is far darker and harsher than the familiar Disney version.

name: Cinderella
description: A gentle girl who endures humiliation from her stepmother and stepsisters until a good fairy sends her to the royal ball. A lost glass slipper becomes the key to her happy ending in one of the best-known fairy tales in the world.
fact: Stories about a persecuted stepdaughter appear in the folklore of many different peoples long before Perrault's French version.

name: Snow White
description: A young princess whose beauty stirs the envy of her wicked stepmother the queen, who orders her got rid of. Her refuge with the seven dwarfs and the poisoned apple have made the tale one of the most recognisable stories in world culture.
fact: "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs" was Disney's first feature-length animated film and one of the first in the history of animation.

name: Ariel the Little Mermaid
description: A curious young mermaid who longs to know the human world and is ready to give up her voice for it. Her collection of human trinkets and her reaching for a seemingly unreachable world made her one of the best-loved Disney princesses.
fact: The Disney film is based on Hans Christian Andersen's tale, though Disney's version softens the ending considerably.

name: Elsa
description: The elder of two royal sisters, born with magic over ice and snow that she was taught as a child to suppress and hide. Her road to accepting her own power, and her famous song about freedom, became a cultural phenomenon well beyond children.
fact: Elsa's song from the film won the Oscar for best song and became one of Disney's most recognisable tunes.

name: Simba
description: A lion cub and heir to the throne of the savannah, driven away from his own pride after a tragedy in the family. His growing up, his friendship with Timon and Pumbaa and his eventual return to claim the crown make a classic coming-of-age story.
fact: The plot is often compared to Shakespeare's "Hamlet", a resemblance the film's own makers have acknowledged.

name: Mickey Mouse
description: A cheerful mouse in red shorts and big yellow shoes who became the official emblem of the entire Disney company. His first appearance in a short with synchronised sound counts as a landmark in the history of animation.
fact: Mickey Mouse was originally voiced by the character's own creator, Walt Disney.

name: Donald Duck
description: A hot-tempered, luckless duck in a sailor suit whose unmistakable squawking voice and frequent explosions of rage made him one of Disney's most popular characters. For all his failures, audiences love him for how honestly he feels everything.
fact: Donald Duck was voiced for decades by one and the same actor, Clarence Nash.

name: Goofy
description: A gangling, good-natured but hopelessly clumsy anthropomorphic dog, friend to Mickey Mouse and Donald Duck. His absurd falls and the distinctive holler he lets out on the way down are a hallmark of classic Disney animation.
fact: Before he became a character in his own right, Goofy turned up in cartoons as a nameless spectator in the stands.

name: Bugs Bunny
description: An unflappable grey rabbit with a carrot in his paw who invariably outwits his hapless opponents, the hunter Elmer Fudd among many others. His line "What's up, Doc?" is one of the most quoted in the history of animation.
fact: Animators have said the way Bugs chews his carrot mid-sentence was a nod to a scene in a Clark Gable film.

name: Tom and Jerry
description: The house cat Tom and the crafty mouse Jerry, chasing each other endlessly through alternating victories and defeats with almost no dialogue at all. Their insane pursuits, packed with slapstick, have long been classics of world animation.
fact: For all the brawling, the series won several Academy Awards for short films over the years.

name: Scooby-Doo
description: A large, cowardly Great Dane with a passion for snacks who keeps landing in supernatural scrapes along with a gang of teenage friends. Terrified of ghosts as he is, it is often his accidental help that unmasks the latest "monster".
fact: The character's name was inspired by a line from Frank Sinatra's song Strangers in the Night.

name: Homer Simpson
description: A safety inspector at a nuclear plant in the fictional town of Springfield, known for his love of doughnuts and beer and for rare bad luck. The cry he lets out at each new failure is one of the most recognisable lines in animation.
fact: Homer's cry of "D'oh!" has since been formally added to English dictionaries.

name: Bart Simpson
description: A restless ten-year-old and the biggest troublemaker at Springfield Elementary, devoted to pranks and his skateboard. His cry of "¡Ay, caramba!" and his spiky haircut made him one of the most recognisable cartoon kids in the world.
fact: Bart Simpson has been voiced for decades, without a break, by the actress Nancy Cartwright.

name: Peter Griffin
description: The explosive, dim-witted head of a household in the fictional town of Quahog, devoted to beer and to serial brawls with a giant chicken. The show runs on his absurd stunts and the endless pop-culture references he throws in mid-scene.
fact: In the original, Peter Griffin is voiced by the show's own creator, Seth MacFarlane.

name: Eric Cartman
description: One of the four boys from the town of South Park, known for his short fuse, his manipulation and his constant selfish schemes to get rich. His cutting remarks and total lack of tact make him the most scandalous character on the show.
fact: The show's creators, Trey Parker and Matt Stone, voice Cartman and most of the other characters themselves.

name: Rick Sanchez
description: A cynical genius inventor who travels between parallel universes with his grandson Morty aboard a spaceship he built himself. His drinking, black humour and contempt for every norm do not stop him being the smartest being in the multiverse.
fact: His name and manner partly parody Doctor Emmett Brown from "Back to the Future".

name: Bender
description: A cynical humanoid robot from the thirtieth century, built to bend metal girders and dreaming of fame and easy money. His taste for cigars, beer and petty scams sits alongside an unexpected loyalty to his friends Fry and Leela.
fact: His full name is Bender Bending Rodríguez, and his serial number turns up in the show's jokes again and again.

name: SpongeBob SquarePants
description: A relentlessly cheerful sea sponge who works as a fry cook at the Krusty Krab on the floor of the Pacific and loves his job more than anything on Earth. His childlike innocence keeps colliding with his grumpy neighbour Squidward and his best friend Patrick.
fact: The show's creator, Stephen Hillenburg, was a marine biologist and an animator before he ever made it.

name: Patrick Star
description: A pink starfish who lives under a rock on the ocean floor and is SpongeBob's best friend. His phenomenal stupidity and peculiar logic land the two of them in ridiculous but very funny trouble on a regular basis.
fact: For all the dimness he displays, in the odd episode Patrick unexpectedly shows flashes of genius.

name: Shrek
description: A grumbling green ogre who wants nothing but solitude in his swamp and is dragged into rescuing a princess to get his peace back. Built on parodies of classic fairy-tale clichés, his story became one of the highest-grossing animated franchises ever.
fact: The character comes from a picture book by William Steig, though the studio reworked him a great deal.

name: Donkey
description: A tireless talking donkey who literally cannot stay quiet for a second and forces himself on Shrek as a best friend against the ogre's wishes. His endless chatter and cheerful naivety eventually become a genuine support for the gruff ogre.
fact: The comedian Eddie Murphy voiced Donkey, and his improvisation shaped much of the character.

name: Puss in Boots
description: A charming swordfighting cat in boots and a feathered hat, sent at first to kill Shrek and ending up as his loyal companion. His famous trick of turning on huge, tearful sad eyes is one of the most recognisable moments in the whole franchise.
fact: The character comes from the classic European fairy tale, but Antonio Banderas voiced him as a Spanish adventurer.

name: Buzz Lightyear
description: A toy space ranger with pop-out wings and a laser, sincerely convinced that he is a real hero and not a product off a shop shelf. His rivalry and then friendship with the cowboy Woody drives the plot of Pixar's first feature film.
fact: Buzz's line "To infinity and beyond!" became one of Pixar's most recognisable catchphrases.

name: Sheriff Woody
description: A rag cowboy with a pull-string in his back, for years the favourite toy of a boy named Andy until Buzz Lightyear arrived. His fear of losing his owner's affection and his care for the other toys are the emotional centre of the franchise.
fact: Woody is voiced by Tom Hanks in every film in the series.

name: Lightning McQueen
description: A young and arrogant race car dreaming of the championship cup, who gets stranded in the sleepy roadside town of Radiator Springs. Getting to know its oddball residents teaches him to value friendship above personal glory.
fact: The number 95 on Lightning's side is a nod to 1995, the year Pixar's first feature film came out.

name: WALL-E
description: A small robot who has spent centuries alone clearing rubbish on an abandoned Earth and collecting the odd human trinkets he finds. Meeting a sleek scouting robot named EVE changes both his quiet life and the fate of all humanity.
fact: Almost half the film passes without a single spoken human line.

name: Po
description: A pudgy, clumsy panda who works in his father's noodle shop while dreaming of kung fu, and is unexpectedly chosen as the legendary Dragon Warrior. Mocked by the masters, his persistence and good heart still turn him into a real hero of the valley.
fact: Po was voiced in the original version by the actor Jack Black.

name: Minions
description: Small yellow capsule-shaped creatures who have served the most varied villains for thousands of years and love bananas above all else. Their gibberish language and chaotic devotion to whoever is in charge made them among the most recognisable cartoon characters today.
fact: Minion speech is a mix of real languages and invented nonsense, recorded by the directors themselves.

name: Pikachu
description: A yellow mouse-like creature that zaps its opponents with electricity and became the official face of the entire Pokémon franchise. Loyal companion to the trainer Ash Ketchum, it refuses to evolve in order to stay itself.
fact: The name Pikachu comes from Japanese sound words for a mouse's squeak and an electric spark.

name: Mario
description: A short, moustachioed Italian plumber in a red cap who rescues Princess Peach from the dragon Bowser over and over again. His jumps, power-up mushrooms and coins became the foundation of the best-selling video game series in the industry.
fact: The character was first called simply Jumpman and was renamed Mario after the landlord of Nintendo's office in America.

name: Sonic
description: A bright blue hedgehog who runs at supersonic speed, collects golden rings and stands against the evil genius Doctor Robotnik. Created as Sega's answer to Mario's popularity, he became the emblem of the company's whole gaming platform.
fact: Tapping his foot impatiently became Sonic's signature animation whenever the player leaves him alone for too long.

name: Lara Croft
description: A British aristocrat and archaeologist who explores ancient tombs and temples around the world in search of artefacts and dangerous secrets. Her twin pistols and athletic agility made her one of the first truly iconic heroines in video games.
fact: Early models of the character were built within the graphical limits of the day, and the resulting body proportions divided fans.

name: Geralt of Rivia
description: A professional monster slayer who went through magical mutation for his inhuman strength, speed and white hair. His moral ambiguity and his eye for the shades of grey between good and evil make him one of the most complex heroes in modern fantasy.
fact: The character first appeared in a short story by the Polish writer Andrzej Sapkowski, not in a computer game.

name: Naruto Uzumaki
description: A loud, stubborn young ninja of the village of Konoha, sealed from birth with a mighty fox demon inside him and dreaming of leading the village one day. His refusal to ever give up and his loyalty to his friends made him one of manga's best-loved heroes.
fact: His favourite dish, ramen noodles, has become an unofficial symbol of the whole franchise.

name: Son Goku
description: A simple-hearted and extraordinarily strong fighter of alien origin, who grows from a naive boy with a monkey tail into the defender of the whole Earth. His endless drive to get stronger and his hunger for honest duels defined a whole genre of adventure manga.
fact: The character owes much to the Monkey King Sun Wukong from the classic Chinese novel "Journey to the West".

name: Monkey D. Luffy
description: The irrepressible captain of a pirate crew whose body stretches like rubber after he accidentally ate a Devil Fruit. His dream of finding the legendary treasure One Piece and becoming King of the Pirates drives one of the best-selling manga in the world.
fact: Luffy's straw hat was a gift from the pirate Shanks, and he promised to return it one day.

name: Sailor Moon
meta: warrior girl in a sailor suit
description: An ordinary Japanese schoolgirl who transforms into a brave warrior in a sailor suit to defend Earth from cosmic villains. Together with the other guardian girls she fights with the power of love and lunar magic, which made the show a classic of the magical-girl genre.
fact: Her fellow guardians are named after the planets of the solar system, and each one's magic depends on her planet.

name: Totoro
description: An enormous furry forest spirit, something between an owl and a cat, visible only to the children who happen to move in next to his wood. His wordless kindness and the umbrella in the rain are among the most recognisable images in Ghibli's animation.
fact: Totoro's silhouette became the official logo of Studio Ghibli itself.

name: Hello Kitty
description: A white anthropomorphic cat with a red bow on her ear, always drawn without a mouth so that anyone can imagine her mood for themselves. Created by the Japanese company Sanrio, she became one of the most recognisable and commercially successful characters in pop culture.
fact: According to Sanrio's official biography she is not a cat at all, but a little English girl named Kitty White.

name: Walter White
description: A mild-mannered high-school chemistry teacher who, after a terminal diagnosis, starts cooking ultra-pure methamphetamine to leave money for his family. His slow shift from quiet educator to ruthless drug kingpin is one of television's most piercing transformations.
fact: His alias in the criminal world, Heisenberg, is a nod to the famous quantum physicist.

name: Jesse Pinkman
description: Walter White's wayward former pupil, pulled by his old teacher into cooking methamphetamine and walking his own painful road through it. For all his coarse slang and naive mistakes, he is the one who keeps a remnant of conscience as his partner falls.
fact: The plan was originally to write him out in the first season, but Aaron Paul's performance changed the writers' minds.

name: Tyrion Lannister
description: A cynical and phenomenally well-read member of the mighty House Lannister, who has spent his whole life fighting his own family's contempt for his height. His sharp mind and knack for finding a way out of hopeless situations made him a favourite of the saga.
fact: The character is famous for his love of wine, and Peter Dinklage won several Emmy awards for playing him.

name: Jon Snow
meta: bastard commander of the Night's Watch
description: The illegitimate son of the Lord of the North, serving in the Night's Watch at the edge of the known world and facing the threat beyond the Wall. His strict sense of duty and his torn, contradictory fate make him a central figure of "A Song of Ice and Fire".
fact: The line "You know nothing, Jon Snow" is one of the most quoted in the entire franchise.

name: Daenerys Targaryen
description: The last of a deposed royal dynasty, raised in exile and coming into command of three dragons. Her path from a powerless girl to a formidable ruler set on reclaiming her ancestors' throne is one of the saga's central storylines.
fact: Daenerys's three dragons hatched from petrified eggs that had long been taken for nothing but an ancient relic.

name: Sheldon Cooper
description: A brilliant but socially hopeless theoretical physicist who lives by a strict timetable and his own unbending rules of conduct. His deafness to sarcasm, his passion for comic books and his designated spot on the sofa supply most of the show's jokes.
fact: His signature ritual is knocking three times on a door and repeating the name of whoever is inside.

name: Doctor Gregory House
description: A brilliant but unbearably cynical diagnostician, limping from an old leg injury and preferring brutal honesty to polite lies. His unorthodox treatments and his famous line about everybody lying made the show one of the most recognisable medical dramas.
fact: The character was conceived largely as a modern Sherlock Holmes, transplanted into a hospital.

name: Michael Scott
description: The manager of a backwater branch of a paper company, desperate to be everyone's friend and forever putting his foot in it. His misplaced jokes and naive need to be liked make him at once the most excruciating and the most touching boss on television.
fact: The character is based on the British original of "The Office", where Ricky Gervais played the equivalent manager.

name: Joey Tribbiani
description: A charming but not especially bright New York actor who will do anything for a part and absolutely will not share his food. His trademark chat-up line and his touching loyalty to his friends made him one of the best-loved characters in the cult sitcom.
fact: After "Friends" ended, the character got his own spin-off series, "Joey", which lasted two seasons.

name: Dexter Morgan
description: A blood spatter analyst with the Miami police who hides carefully controlled murderous urges behind a courteous mask. Following his foster father's strict "code", he kills only other killers who slipped through justice, balancing two lives at once.
fact: The character first appeared in a series of novels by the writer Jeff Lindsay rather than being invented for television.

name: Thomas Shelby
description: The charismatic, calculating leader of the criminal Shelby family, who came through the trenches of the First World War and turned a street gang into a genuine empire. The gang's trademark tweed caps gave the whole franchise its name.
fact: Cillian Murphy plays the part, and a gang by that nickname really did operate in Birmingham around the turn of the 20th century.

name: Eleven
description: A mysterious girl with a shaved head and a number tattooed on her wrist, escaped from a secret laboratory and armed with powerful telekinetic abilities. Her friendship with a group of teenagers in the town of Hawkins, and her love of waffles, anchor the show.
fact: She is played by the young actress Millie Bobby Brown, who had to shave her head completely for the role.

name: Wednesday Addams
description: The pale, unflappable daughter of a family devoted to everything macabre, who treats torture and funerals as ordinary entertainment. Her ice-cold sarcasm and utterly expressionless face made her one of pop culture's most recognisable gothic heroines.
fact: She first appeared in Charles Addams's newspaper cartoons, where for years she did not even have a name.

name: Mr. Bean
description: An absurd and almost entirely silent oddball who lands in one comic disaster after another through sheer clumsiness and his own strange logic. His faithful companion is a teddy bear called Teddy, and his little yellow car is part of the picture.
fact: Rowan Atkinson built the character so that the jokes would work for audiences in any country without translation.

name: Barbie
description: A slender doll with a flawless wardrobe and dozens of careers, from astronaut to president, created by the American company Mattel. Over the decades she became both the best-selling toy in the world and a focus of argument about ideals of female beauty.
fact: According to the brand's own lore, the doll's full name is Barbara Millicent Roberts.

name: Optimus Prime
description: The noble leader of the Autobots, a race of robots who turn into vehicles, most often shown in the form of a blue truck. His long war against the villainous Megatron and the Decepticons became the basis of one of the longest-lived toy franchises.
fact: The character's classic voice in the cartoon series and the first films belonged to the actor Peter Cullen.

name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
description: Four anthropomorphic mutant turtles trained in martial arts by a wise rat sensei and living in the sewers of New York. Named after Renaissance artists, they fight crime while remaining devoted to ordinary pizza.
fact: They first appeared in an independent black-and-white comic conceived as a parody of other superhero teams.

name: Cheburashka
description: A strange big-eared creature of a species unknown to science, found in a crate of oranges and settling into a telephone box. His friendship with Gena the Crocodile and the House of Friendship they build made him a favourite of generations of Soviet and Russian children.
fact: His name comes from a Russian word for tumbling over: he kept falling down out of clumsiness.

name: Gena the Crocodile
meta: a crocodile who works at the zoo
description: A well-mannered crocodile who took a job at the zoo playing a crocodile and plays the accordion in the evenings out of loneliness. It is his advertisement looking for friends that brings him Cheburashka and begins their long friendship.
fact: Gena's song about a birthday coming only once a year is one of the most recognisable tunes in Soviet animation.

name: The Wolf from "Nu, Pogodi!"
description: A hooligan wolf in a striped sailor's shirt, endlessly and unsuccessfully chasing a quick-witted hare. With practically no spoken dialogue at all, the series became one of the best-known classics of Soviet animation.
fact: The wolf's catchphrase, "Well, hare, just you wait!", comes in nearly every episode and gave the series its title.

name: Matroskin the Cat
description: A level-headed talking cat who moves to the village of Prostokvashino together with a boy called Uncle Fyodor and his parents. His practicality, his devotion to the cow Murka and his famous line about working together made him a favourite of Soviet animation.
fact: In the Prostokvashino films Matroskin speaks with the voice of the actor Oleg Tabakov.

name: Dunno
description: A hapless, boastful little fellow from Flower Town who constantly takes on jobs he understands nothing about. His many failures and adventures across Nikolay Nosov's trilogy teach young readers by way of the hero's own mistakes.
fact: In the final part of the trilogy, "Dunno on the Moon", the little people fly into space and land in a world of money and profit.

name: Buratino
description: A mischievous wooden boy with a long nose, carved by the old organ-grinder Papa Carlo out of a talking log. His golden key and his adventures in the company of the cat Basilio and the fox Alice are classics of Soviet children's literature.
fact: Alexey Tolstoy's book is a Russian retelling and reworking of the Italian tale of Pinocchio.

name: Doctor Aybolit
description: The kindest of doctors, who treats animals from all over the world and sets off for Africa to save ailing elephants, hippos and jackals. His readiness to help any creature at all made him a symbol of selfless kindness in Soviet children's literature.
fact: The good doctor is thought to be modelled on an acquaintance of Chukovsky's, the Vilnius physician Tsemakh Shabad, who treated the poor for free.

name: Baba Yaga
description: A mysterious old sorceress who lives deep in the forest in a hut standing on chicken legs and flies about in a mortar with a broom. Depending on the tale she either helps the hero with wise advice or becomes the main danger he has to outwit.
fact: In the tales the hut on chicken legs only turns to face the hero once he has spoken a particular charm.

name: Koschei the Deathless
description: A gaunt, malevolent sorcerer of Russian folktales whose death is hidden in the point of a needle, inside an egg, inside a duck, inside a hare. An abductor of princesses and the eternal enemy of the heroes, he stands for evil that cannot be beaten the ordinary way.
fact: The old Russian word behind his name meant a thin, bony man, or a captive.

name: Ilya Muromets
description: A mighty peasant's son who lay motionless on the stove for thirty-three years before miraculously receiving the strength of a hero. Made the chief defender of Kievan Rus in the Russian epic songs, he remains a model of martial valour and justice.
fact: The epic hero is thought to be based on a real monk, Ilya of the Caves, whose relics are kept in the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra.

name: Kolobok
description: A round, rosy bun that an old woman baked from the last of her flour, and which promptly escaped from the windowsill and the old couple. On the road it slips away from a hare, a wolf and a bear while singing a boastful little song, until a cunning fox gets it.
fact: Tales of an edible runaway turn up in the folklore of many peoples, the famous English gingerbread man among them.

name: Ostap Bender
description: A charming swindler and grand schemer who claims to know four hundred comparatively honest ways of taking other people's money. His hunt for diamonds hidden in one of twelve chairs became one of the best-loved satirical stories in Soviet literature.
fact: Many of his aphorisms have long lived on in Russian as sayings in their own right, quite apart from the novel.

name: Stierlitz
description: A Soviet intelligence officer who spent years working in Nazi Germany under the identity of a senior SS officer. His composure and his gift for calculating the enemy's next move made him perhaps the best-known spy in Soviet culture.
fact: The character became the hero of an enormous body of jokes, all playing on how unshakeably calm he stays.

name: Danila Bagrov
description: A young man back from the army who is drawn into his older brother's criminal quarrels in the St Petersburg of the nineties. His few words, his own private sense of justice and the cassette player in his pocket made him a symbol of post-Soviet cinema.
fact: His line asking where real strength lies has long since become a catchphrase living on without the film.

name: Shurik
description: A modest, inquisitive student in spectacles who lands in one comic predicament after another, from a construction brigade to an accidental meeting with a gang of bride-snatchers. His naive honesty among crooks is the hallmark of several cult Soviet comedies.
fact: The same actor, Alexander Demyanenko, played the character under this name in several different Gaidai films.
wiki_en: Operation Y and Other Shurik's Adventures

name: Comrade Sukhov
meta: Red Army soldier in the desert
description: A demobilised Red Army soldier who dreams of getting home to his wife but finds himself minding the harem of a fugitive warlord along the way. His unhurried good sense and his letters to the distant Katerina Matveyevna are endlessly quoted.
fact: Russian cosmonauts traditionally watch the film before a launch, as part of their pre-flight ritual.

name: Gleb Zheglov
description: An uncompromising detective in the Moscow criminal police of the post-war years, ready to step over the formalities of the law to catch a criminal. His argument with his young partner about whether the end justifies the means is the heart of a cult television film.
fact: Zheglov was played by Vladimir Vysotsky, for whom the part was one of the last of his life.
wiki_en: The Meeting Place Cannot Be Changed

name: Eugene Onegin
description: A young nobleman so disenchanted with life that he turns down the sincere love of a provincial girl, Tatyana, for the cold boredom of society. His inner emptiness and belated remorse made him the model of the "superfluous man" in Russian literature.
fact: Pushkin worked on the novel in verse for more than seven years, gradually changing his original plan for the plot.

name: Rodion Raskolnikov
description: A poor St Petersburg student who resolves to murder an old pawnbroker in order to test his own theory about the right of the strong individual. His agonising inner torment after the crime is the psychological core of one of Dostoevsky's great novels.
fact: His theory dividing people into the "ordinary" and those "with a right" has fuelled countless philosophical arguments.

name: Anna Karenina
meta: society lady in a tragic love
description: A married aristocrat of high St Petersburg society whose passionate love for the officer Vronsky brings her into conflict with her family and under the condemnation of society. Her tragic fate is one of literature's most famous studies of love and morality.
fact: The novel's famous opening sentence about happy and unhappy families has long been an aphorism of its own.

name: Woland
description: A mysterious foreign professor of black magic who arrives in the Moscow of the 1930s with a retinue of demons to hand out a justice of his own. His famous line that manuscripts do not burn is among the most recognisable quotations in Russian literature.
fact: Bulgakov's novel was published only decades after his death, and at first in a heavily cut version.

name: Behemoth the Cat
description: An enormous black cat in Woland's retinue, able to turn into a portly man and devoted to chess and insolent jokes. His escapades in Soviet Moscow, from riding a tram to firing a revolver, are among the most memorable scenes in the novel.
fact: His name points to the biblical monster Behemoth, mentioned in the Book of Job.

name: Masha
description: An energetic, unstoppable little girl who has settled in next door to a good-natured circus Bear thoroughly worn out by her pranks. Her boundless energy and her gift for turning any situation into chaos made the Russian cartoon a hit far beyond its home country.
fact: Individual episodes have collected billions of views on YouTube, and the series has been translated into dozens of languages.

name: Krash
description: An impulsive round rabbit always in a hurry somewhere, who far prefers sport and risky ventures to sitting still and thinking. He is one of the leads in a Russian cartoon about round little animals that became a landmark of the country's animation in the 2000s.
fact: Every character's design is built out of circles, and the Russian title blends the words for "funny" and "little balls".

name: Luntik
meta: little one fallen from the Moon
description: A furry little creature born on the Moon who fell to Earth by accident, straight into a forest pond, where insects found him and brought him up. His good-natured wonder at everything new made the series one of Russia's most popular cartoons for small children.
fact: His name comes straight from the Russian word for the Moon, luna, which is where the story says he came from.

name: Uncle Styopa
description: An extraordinarily tall and good-natured giant from Sergey Mikhalkov's poems, who in the sequels becomes a policeman on traffic duty. His readiness to help, from pulling people out of the water to putting out fires, made him a model hero of Soviet children's verse.
fact: Mikhalkov wrote about Uncle Styopa for nearly half a century, from the first poem in the thirties to a late one about him as a veteran.

name: Old Man Hottabych
description: A mighty genie who spent thousands of years imprisoned in a clay jug and is set free by a Soviet schoolboy called Volka. His old-fashioned oriental speech and his naive attempts to make sense of Soviet life supply one comic situation after another.
fact: The book owes a great deal to an English novel about a genie, with the action moved to Soviet Moscow.

name: Elektronik
description: A robot boy built from a photograph of the schoolboy Seryozha Syroyezhkin and indistinguishable from him, which lets the two swap places. His friendship with the other children and his slow acquisition of almost human feelings anchor a famous Soviet book and film.
fact: The song "Winged Swings" from the television film about him became one of the best-known Soviet children's songs.

name: Obi-Wan Kenobi
description: A Jedi master, mentor first to Anakin Skywalker and later to his son Luke. Wise and restrained, he would rather negotiate than fight, but handles a lightsaber superbly when he has to. One of the few Jedi knights to survive the fall of the Order.
fact: Alec Guinness, who played Obi-Wan in the original trilogy, was at first rather cool about taking a part in a science fiction film.

name: Emperor Palpatine
description: A secretive politician who spent years weaving a conspiracy behind the mask of Chancellor of the Republic, until he declared himself Emperor. A mighty dark lord of the Sith commanding the destructive lightning of the Force, he is cunning and absolute power in one.
fact: The Emperor first appeared on screen only in "The Empire Strikes Back", in a brief holographic message to Darth Vader.

name: Boba Fett
description: A taciturn bounty hunter in unmistakable armour, one of the most cult-worshipped supporting characters in the saga. He works for the Empire and hunts Han Solo, but his first loyalty is to his own profit. His air of mystery earned him a string of spin-offs.
fact: Boba Fett debuted not in a film but in an animated segment of the television "Star Wars Holiday Special" of 1978.

name: Darth Maul
description: A horned Sith warrior with war paint across his face and a double-bladed lightsaber, silent and lethal. Apprentice to Darth Sidious, he serves as his master's hidden blade in the shadow of political intrigue. A short appearance in "The Phantom Menace" made him iconic.
fact: Darth Maul was meant to be a throwaway character, but audience affection kept pulling him back into new stories.

name: Kylo Ren
description: A knight of the dark side torn apart inside, desperate to prove his loyalty to the new Order. He wears a mask and carries a modified lightsaber with a crossguard, and fights with a hot, impulsive temper. His fate is bound up with the legacy of the Skywalkers.
fact: The crackle and unsteady hum of Kylo Ren's blade were designed to convey the instability of its crystal.

name: Rey Skywalker
description: A solitary scrap collector from the desert planet Jakku in whom an enormous potential in the Force unexpectedly awakens. She takes up a lightsaber and the path of the Jedi while searching for her place in the galaxy and her link to the past.
fact: Before she ever picks up a lightsaber, Rey spends much of the film handling an ordinary quarterstaff with great skill.

name: Jar Jar Binks
description: A clumsy, talkative inhabitant of the underwater Gungan city on the planet Naboo, swept by accident into great political events. His comic behaviour and mangled speech clash sharply with the serious tone of the rest of the saga.
fact: Jar Jar was one of the first fully computer-generated characters with a large role in live-action cinema; on set he was played by Ahmed Best.

name: Magneto
description: One of Marvel's most powerful mutants, able to command metal by thought alone. A survivor of the Holocaust, he became a committed fighter for mutant rights, sometimes by means that make him Professor X's ideological opponent rather than a plain villain.
fact: Magneto's real name is Max Eisenhardt, though his biography has been rewritten more than once across different versions.

name: Professor X
description: One of the strongest telepaths on the planet, who uses his gift not for power but to protect mutants and work towards peace with humans. He founded a school for gifted youngsters that became the home of the X-Men, and he leads from a wheelchair.
fact: Professor X and Magneto were conceived as two opposed philosophies in the struggle for minority rights.

name: Mystique
description: A blue-skinned mutant who can take on the appearance of any person, which makes her an unmatched spy and assassin. Her loyalty wavers constantly between Magneto and her own aims, and she is one of the least predictable figures in the X-Men universe.
fact: For the films, actresses had to sit for hours in make-up to get Mystique's distinctive blue scaled skin.

name: Doctor Doom
description: A genius scientist and sorcerer who made himself absolute ruler of the fictional country of Latveria. An accident left his face hidden behind a metal mask forever, and his pride will not let him admit anyone's superiority in either science or magic.
fact: Doctor Doom is formally the monarch of a sovereign state, which makes him a rare comic-book villain with diplomatic immunity.

name: Doctor Strange
description: A once brilliant but insufferably vain neurosurgeon who went looking for a cure after his hands were ruined and found mastery of the mystic arts instead. As Sorcerer Supreme he defends reality from interdimensional threats with the Eye of Agamotto and a cloak of levitation.
fact: The artist Steve Ditko experimented with psychedelic visual effects that later became the signature look of magic in comics.

name: Ant-Man
description: A superhero whose special suit carries Pym particles, letting him change size in an instant from giant to microscopic. Different heroes have worn the name over the years, among them the scientist Hank Pym and the reformed thief Scott Lang, and a helmet lets him command armies of ants.
fact: The same Pym particles also work the other way: in the comics Hank Pym operated as Giant-Man.

name: Star-Lord
description: Peter Quill, an Earthling raised among space smugglers after being abducted from Earth as a child. He leads the ragtag crew of the Guardians of the Galaxy, mixing bravado with real devotion to his new friends, and never parts with his old player and its tapes.
fact: Star-Lord's player of Earth hits became the basis of the "Awesome Mix" soundtrack albums, which were real-world hits too.

name: Rocket Raccoon
description: The result of brutal genetic experiments that turned an ordinary raccoon into a cynical, hot-tempered master of weapons and machinery. Small as he is, he is one of the deadliest fighters among the Guardians of the Galaxy, and his rudeness hides deep damage and a fierce attachment to his few friends.
fact: His name was suggested by The Beatles song "Rocky Raccoon", a favourite of his creator, the writer Bill Mantlo.

name: Venom
description: An alien symbiote that bonds with a human host and grants him enormous strength, regeneration and the ability to change shape. Long an enemy of Spider-Man, he grew into a more complicated antihero with rules of his own. The black viscous body and bared fangs are unmistakable.
fact: The Venom symbiote first appeared as Spider-Man's new black costume, before it became a character of its own.

name: Green Goblin
description: The wealthy industrialist Norman Osborn, turned by his own experiment into a deranged villain with a flying glider and an arsenal of pumpkin bombs. He is one of Spider-Man's chief and most personal enemies, and his ghastly green-and-purple mask is among the most recognisable images in comics.
fact: Over the decades several successors have worn the Green Goblin's mask, including Osborn's own son.

name: The Penguin
description: Oswald Cobblepot, the eccentric crime magnate of Gotham, who hides a sharp mind behind the figure of an absurd little man with an umbrella-cane. He owns the Iceberg Lounge nightclub and runs a double life through it, between legitimate business and crime. One of Batman's oldest foes.
fact: For all the nickname, the Penguin has no bird-like powers whatsoever, only a love of umbrellas and theatrical effect.

name: Two-Face
description: Harvey Dent, once Gotham's uncompromising district attorney, became obsessed with chance after an acid attack and now flips a coin to decide people's fates. Half his face is ruined, a picture of the split between good and evil in his mind. A tragic figure among Batman's villains.
fact: Two-Face's special coin, clean on one side and scarred on the other, became his defining symbol.

name: Riddler
description: Edward Nigma, a vain criminal genius obsessed with puzzles, word games and intellectual duels with Batman. He leaves riddles at his crime scenes as though he simply cannot resist showing off his own cleverness. The green suit covered in question marks is his permanent signature.
fact: The Riddler's name is itself a pun: Edward Nigma sounds out as "enigma".

name: Bane
description: Raised in the brutal prison of Peña Duro, Bane is one of the few opponents able to break Batman not only by outthinking him but by sheer physical force. He uses the drug Venom, which multiplies his muscular power. A strategist and a tactician rather than a mere bruiser.
fact: It was Bane who, in the comics of the 1990s, literally broke Batman's back for the first time in the franchise.

name: Alfred Pennyworth
description: The faithful butler of Wayne Manor, who became a father to young Bruce after his parents were killed. He helps Batman both with the household and with the technology in the cave, and remains his voice of conscience and common sense. His dry English humour lightens the gloom of Gotham.
fact: In the early comics Alfred was conceived as a rather comic, portly figure; the familiar trim version came later.

name: Aquaman
description: Arthur Curry, half human and half Atlantean, can breathe underwater, command the creatures of the sea and calls on superhuman strength. The rightful ruler of the undersea kingdom of Atlantis, he is torn between two worlds, land and ocean. One of the founders of the Justice League.
fact: Aquaman was long dismissed as a "silly" hero, until the films showed what he is actually capable of in a fight.

name: The Flash
description: A hero who gained the power to move faster than sound after an accident with chemicals and a lightning strike. Several characters have carried the name over the years, the best known being the forensic scientist Barry Allen. His link to the Speed Force even lets him travel in time.
fact: The original 1940s Flash, Jay Garrick, wore a winged helmet in a nod to the helmet of Mercury, the ancient messenger god.

name: Green Lantern
description: The bearer of a power ring that can materialise any object by force of will, and a member of the intergalactic Green Lantern Corps that keeps order across the universe. The best-known bearer on Earth is the pilot Hal Jordan. The ring's one weakness is the colour yellow.
fact: The DC universe has counted thousands of Green Lanterns, each guarding a sector of space of their own.

name: Lex Luthor
description: A genius scientist and billionaire from Metropolis whose hatred of Superman rests on the conviction that humanity needs no alien saviour. He works through legitimate business and politics as much as through outright criminal schemes. One of the cleverest and most dangerous men in the DC universe.
fact: In the comics Lex Luthor at one point actually held the office of President of the United States.

name: Darkseid
description: The all-powerful lord of the grim planet Apokolips, obsessed with finding the Anti-Life Equation that would strip every thinking being of free will. One of the mightiest and coldest villains in the DC universe, set against the Justice League and the New Gods.
fact: Darkseid was created by the legendary artist Jack Kirby as part of his sweeping epic about the New Gods.

name: Deadshot
description: Floyd Lawton, the deadliest marksman in the DC universe, a contract killer who claims he never misses. He works for money and also as part of the conscripted Suicide Squad in exchange for a lighter sentence. Behind the cynical front lies a complicated bond with his own daughter.
fact: The character did not start out in a title of his own: he first appeared in a Batman comic.

name: Atticus Finch
description: A middle-aged lawyer in a small town in the American South, raising two children alone and taking on the defence of a Black man before a racist court. He is quiet dignity, honesty and moral steadiness in the face of the whole town's pressure.
fact: Readers' polls have repeatedly named Atticus Finch one of the greatest heroes of 20th-century American literature.

name: Jay Gatsby
description: An enigmatic new-money millionaire who throws roaring parties at his Long Island mansion for one purpose only: to win back a lost love from his youth. Behind the glitter and the display is a man stuck in an idealised past. A symbol of the American dream and of its underside.
fact: At his own loud parties Gatsby himself barely appears among the guests, watching what happens from the side.

name: Scarlett O'Hara
description: The wilful, pragmatic daughter of a planter in pre-war Georgia, whose life is overturned by the Civil War. She will resort to any trick and any sacrifice to save her family estate of Tara and herself. One of the most vivid and contradictory heroines in American literature.
fact: Her famous line, "I'll think about it tomorrow", recurs through the novel as she puts hard decisions off.

name: Rhett Butler
description: A charming dealer and blockade runner who profits from other people's misfortunes during the Civil War, yet is secretly capable of real passion. His wit and clear-eyed view of the world clash with the romantic illusions around him. One of American culture's best-known romantic heroes.
fact: Rhett Butler's closing line in the 1939 film became one of the most quoted lines in the history of Hollywood.

name: Jane Eyre
description: An orphan raised in a harsh charity school who becomes a governess at the gloomy estate of Thornfield, where a difficult love for its master awaits her. Poor and lowly as she is, her sense of her own worth never bends. One of the first strong heroines in English literature.
fact: Charlotte Brontë's novel was first published under a man's pen name, Currer Bell.

name: Mr Darcy
description: A proud, reserved English landowner whose coldness at balls conceals shyness and deep feeling. His difficult relationship with Elizabeth Bennet is built on getting past mutual prejudice and wounded pride. One of the most famous romantic heroes in English literature.
fact: The wet-shirt scene in the BBC's 1995 adaptation became one of the most iconic moments in British television.

name: Elizabeth Bennet
description: The second of five daughters of a not-too-wealthy English gentleman, sharp-minded, independent and given to irony. She is not afraid to defy the conventions of society, or her own prejudices, for the sake of genuine feeling. One of the best-loved heroines in all of English literature.
fact: Jane Austen wrote in her letters that Elizabeth Bennet was as delightful a creature as ever appeared in print.

name: Oliver Twist
description: An orphan from a workhouse whose modest request for more gruel became one of the most famous scenes in English literature. Out on the streets of London, he falls in with a gang of young pickpockets run by the crafty Fagin. A story of poverty and a child's survival in a brutal age.
fact: Dickens published the novel in monthly instalments, which kept readers in suspense for months at a time.

name: Ebenezer Scrooge
description: A hard, grasping old moneylender who despises Christmas and every show of kindness, until three spirits visit him on Christmas Eve. Their visits force him to look again at his whole life and at how he treats other people. One of literature's great emblems of redemption.
fact: The name Scrooge has long since become an ordinary English word for a miser.

name: Dorian Gray
description: A beautiful young man whose painted portrait ages and grows hideous in his place while he himself stays forever young. Freedom from consequences drives him into an ever more depraved life. Oscar Wilde's novel about the price of vanity and the hidden cost of lasting beauty.
fact: Wilde's only novel caused such a scandal in his lifetime that he had to soften several passages for reissue.

name: Doctor Jekyll and Mr Hyde
description: A respectable London doctor who invents a potion that releases the dark side of his personality in the shape of the brutal Mr Hyde. The story of human nature split between reason and primal instinct is a classic of gothic fiction, and the two names are now a byword for a divided character.
fact: People still say "Jekyll and Hyde" to describe someone with two sharply opposed sides to their character.

name: Captain Nemo
description: A mysterious scientist in exile who cut every tie with human society and built the submarine Nautilus, in which he roams the oceans. A brilliant engineer and a misanthrope, his true motives and origins stay hidden for a long time. One of the first great antiheroes of adventure fiction.
fact: A later Jules Verne novel, "The Mysterious Island", reveals Captain Nemo's real name and his past.

name: Robinson Crusoe
description: An English sailor left as the only survivor of a shipwreck on a desert island, where he has years ahead of him. Through work and invention he turns wild nature into something like a civilised household. Daniel Defoe's book is counted among the first English novels and founded a whole genre.
fact: The story is thought to be based on the real sailor Alexander Selkirk, who spent several years alone on an island.

name: Gulliver
description: A ship's surgeon whose fantastic voyages carry him to the land of the tiny Lilliputians, then to the giants of Brobdingnag, then to stranger peoples still. Through his astonishment at these worlds Jonathan Swift mocks the vices of his own society. An early masterpiece of satirical fiction.
fact: In Lilliput, Gulliver is pinned to the ground with thousands of fine threads while he sleeps after the shipwreck.

name: d'Artagnan
description: A young, ambitious Gascon who comes to Paris to become one of the king's musketeers and is soon the close friend of three legendary swordsmen. Brave, hot-headed and as loyal to friendship as to honour. One of the most famous heroes in adventure fiction, created by Alexandre Dumas.
fact: D'Artagnan had a real historical model: a Gascon nobleman and officer of the musketeers in the 17th century.

name: Athos
description: The oldest and most silent of the three musketeers, whose aristocratic reserve hides a heavy secret from his past. A wise mentor to the young d'Artagnan and an unmatched swordsman. Honour and dignity embodied among the heroes of Dumas's novels.
fact: His real name comes out in the course of the novel: he turns out to be the Count de la Fère, with a difficult personal history.

name: Porthos
description: The tallest and physically strongest of the four musketeers, simple-hearted and fond of a good meal and a showy outfit. His bluntness and good nature stand in sharp contrast to the intrigues of court life. A loyal comrade, ready to cover his friends in any fight.
fact: Porthos is the only one of the four who takes sincere pride not in his wits but in his own physical strength.

name: Aramis
description: The most refined and most enigmatic of the musketeers, who dreams of one day leaving soldiering for the church. He combines an aristocrat's exquisite manners with a calculating mind and a master's hand with a sword. In time he becomes the most influential and politically adept of the four.
fact: In Dumas's later novels Aramis makes the most striking career of the four friends, rising to be a powerful church figure.

name: The Count of Monte Cristo
description: Edmond Dantès, a young sailor wrongly convicted and locked in the Château d'If, escapes, finds an immense treasure and returns under a new name. For years he methodically builds a plan of revenge on the men who destroyed his life. One of literature's most famous avengers.
fact: Dumas took his plot from the real story of a French shoemaker who fell victim to a conspiracy of envious acquaintances.

name: Quasimodo
description: The deaf, misshapen bell-ringer of Notre-Dame, hidden from a cruel world inside the cathedral walls since childhood. Behind the frightening face is a tender, devoted soul capable of the most sincere love. One of the most moving characters in Victor Hugo's novel.
fact: He was named after the day he was left at the cathedral: Quasimodo Sunday, the first Sunday after Easter.

name: Esmeralda
description: A young street dancer from a Romani troupe whose beauty and kindness draw the attention of several men in Paris at once, from the bell-ringer to the archdeacon. She loves her freedom and is kind to outcasts, Quasimodo included. Innocence amid the cruelty of Hugo's novel.
fact: Esmeralda has a faithful tame goat called Djali, who appears at her side in almost every scene of the novel.

name: Don Quixote
description: An elderly Spanish gentleman driven mad by tales of chivalry, who imagines himself a knight errant fighting for justice. With his faithful squire Sancho Panza he takes to the road, mistaking windmills for giants. One of literature's most famous and most touching dreamers.
fact: Cervantes's book is considered one of the first and most influential novels in the history of modern European literature.

name: Sancho Panza
description: A simple-hearted peasant who becomes Don Quixote's squire in exchange for the promise of an island to govern. His down-to-earth good sense and folk wisdom are a constant counterweight to his master's mad fantasies. In time a real, touching friendship grows between them.
fact: For all his teasing of his master's naivety, Sancho Panza becomes sincerely attached to Don Quixote and stays with him to the end.

name: Romeo
description: The young scion of the Montague house of Verona, whose ardent love for Juliet of the enemy Capulet family becomes a trial for both clans. Impulsive, romantic and ready for any extreme for the sake of feeling. One of the great symbols of romantic love in world culture.
fact: The name Romeo has long been an everyday word for an ardent romantic suitor.

name: Juliet
