description: The thirteen-year-old daughter of the Capulet family, whose first love for Romeo of the rival Montagues brings tragedy on both houses. She is determined and true to her feelings against her parents' will and her family's feud. One of Shakespeare's best-known tragic heroines.
fact: The famous balcony scene in which Juliet speaks her monologue never actually mentions a balcony in the original text.

name: Hamlet
description: The Prince of Denmark, who learns from his father's ghost that he was murdered and is torn between the thirst for revenge and agonising philosophical doubt. His speeches on life, death and the point of existence made the play one of the most quoted works in world culture.
fact: The speech beginning "To be or not to be" is one of the most recognisable passages in all of English literature.

name: Macbeth
description: A Scottish warlord whose ambition is inflamed by the prophecies of three witches and the urging of his own wife. Murdering the king for the throne draws him into an ever more deranged spiral of violence and paranoia. One of Shakespeare's darkest tragedies about unchecked ambition.
fact: Actors still keep the superstition of never saying the play's name backstage, calling it only "the Scottish play".

name: Othello
description: A successful Black Venetian general whose happy marriage to Desdemona is destroyed by the cunning slander of his envious officer Iago. Jealousy, skilfully stoked by intrigue, drives him to a tragic mistake. One of Shakespeare's most piercing tragedies of trust, betrayal and jealousy.
fact: The name of the scheming Iago from this play has long been a byword for a calculating slanderer.

name: Cipollino
description: A brave little onion boy who leads the struggle of the ordinary fruits and vegetables against the unjust rule of Signor Tomato and the haughty nobility. Cunning, quick-witted and always ready to stand up for the weak. One of the best-known characters in 20th-century Italian children's literature.
fact: Gianni Rodari's tale was loved in the Soviet Union almost more widely than in the author's native Italy.

name: Malvina
description: A doll with blue hair and impeccable manners who lives in the forest and tries to raise the disobedient Buratino by every rule of good conduct. Her lessons in arithmetic and handwriting are a constant source of conflict with the mischievous wooden boy.
fact: Malvina's blue hair has stayed one of the most recognisable details in Soviet book illustration for decades.
wiki_en: The Golden Key, or the Adventures of Buratino

name: Duremar
description: A gangling, gloomy figure in a long frock coat who makes his living selling leeches and works in the service of Karabas-Barabas. His dismal face and endless complaints about life became his trademark in the Soviet cartoons. A minor but instantly recognisable character.
fact: There is no Duremar in the Italian original, "The Adventures of Pinocchio": Alexey Tolstoy invented him himself.
wiki_en: The Golden Key, or the Adventures of Buratino

name: Pierrot
description: The melancholy puppet poet of Karabas-Barabas's theatre, forever sighing over his unreturned love for Malvina. In a white smock with long sleeves he declaims sorrowful verses, a sharp contrast to the cheerful troublemaker Buratino. The classic sad clown, moved into a Soviet fairy tale.
fact: Pierrot goes back to a traditional figure of European theatre: the sad lovelorn clown of the commedia dell'arte.
wiki_en: The Golden Key, or the Adventures of Buratino

name: Karabas-Barabas
description: The bearded, cruel owner of a puppet theatre, who bullies his marionette actors and is obsessed with finding the golden key. His long beard, which keeps catching in doorways, is one of the most recognisable things about him. The chief villain of Alexey Tolstoy's tale.
fact: In the book Karabas-Barabas keeps his puppets in terror with a seven-tailed whip and tucks his beard into his pocket.
wiki_en: The Golden Key, or the Adventures of Buratino

name: Papa Carlo
description: A poor but warm-hearted organ-grinder who carved a talking wooden boy out of a log and became a father to him. He patiently puts up with disobedient Buratino's pranks and goes on caring for him as for his own son. Plain human kindness embodied in Alexey Tolstoy's tale.
fact: Papa Carlo's little room, with a hearth painted on a canvas, hides a secret door into a magical puppet theatre.
wiki_en: The Golden Key, or the Adventures of Buratino

name: Little Red Riding Hood
description: A kind girl sent by her mother through the forest with treats for her sick grandmother, who trustingly falls into conversation with a cunning wolf on the way. One of the best-known tales about naivety and the dangers waiting on the road, told in many versions across Europe.
fact: The best-known literary version of the tale was written down by the French storyteller Charles Perrault in the late 17th century.

name: Emelya
description: The hero of a Russian tale who caught a talking pike and, for letting it go, was given a magic gift: any wish granted at the words "by the pike's command". The stove carries him through the village by itself and the buckets go for water with no hands. Luck won not by labour but by wit and kindness.
fact: The famous stove that Emelya rides around on is one of the most recognisable images in Russian folk tales.

name: Ivan the Fool
description: The youngest and seemingly dimmest of three brothers in Russian tales, mocked by his own family until he turns out to be the kindest, the most honest and, in the end, the luckiest. His apparent simplicity often proves to be practical wisdom. One of the great archetypes of Russian folklore.
fact: Very different stories go under the name of Ivan the Fool, held together only by the type of hero at their centre.

name: Vasilisa the Beautiful
description: A heroine of Russian tales who combines rare beauty with wisdom and magical skills, left to her by her dead mother in the form of a treasured little helper doll. She passes trials at Baba Yaga's hut and outlives the spite of her stepmother's daughters.
fact: Across different tales the name Vasilisa the Beautiful sits alongside a similar figure, Vasilisa the Wise.

name: Zmey Gorynych
description: The fire-breathing three-headed monster of Russian epics and tales, who carries people off and holds whole villages in terror. Defeating him is traditionally the great trial set for a warrior hero. One of the most recognisable fantastic figures in Slavic folklore.
fact: The number of heads varies between tales and epic songs: versions run from three all the way up to twelve.

name: The Firebird
description: A fabulous bird with glowing golden, flame-like plumage, for a single feather of which heroes set out on dangerous journeys. Catching it is often part of an impossible royal errand along with other marvels. One of the most beautiful and mysterious images in Russian folklore.
fact: The Firebird inspired Igor Stravinsky's famous ballet of the same name in the early 20th century.

name: Morozko
description: The stern but fair spirit of the winter forest, who tests a stepdaughter and the stepmother's own daughter out in the cold and rewards patience and courtesy generously. He is the basis of a famous Soviet fairy-tale film and one of the oldest figures of the winter tales.
fact: The 1964 Soviet film "Morozko" became a Christmas tradition in the Czech Republic, where it is shown on television every year.

name: The Snow Maiden
description: A girl moulded out of snow by an old couple and brought to life, whose fate is bound to the cold: when the warmth comes she melts or flies away. In the later tradition she became Grandfather Frost's constant companion at New Year. One of the most recognisable winter figures in Russian culture.
fact: She became Grandfather Frost's permanent helper at New Year celebrations comparatively recently, in Soviet times.

name: Grandfather Frost
description: A kindly white-bearded old man in a long fur coat with a staff, who brings children presents at New Year and, by settled legend, lives in Veliky Ustyug. The figure began as a harsh spirit of winter and frost and softened over time into a generous giver of gifts.
fact: Grandfather Frost's official residence in Russia is the town of Veliky Ustyug, in the Vologda region.

name: Moydodyr
description: A living, talking washstand, "chief of the washbasins and commander of the sponges", who chases a filthy, slovenly boy until he finally agrees to wash. A funny, instructive tale in verse that teaches children to love being clean. One of the most quoted characters in Russian children's writing.
fact: Moydodyr's lines about the need to wash are still quoted by parents in Russia when getting children used to washing.

name: The Monster Cockroach
description: An ordinary cockroach who terrifies every animal in the forest with his fearsome whiskers and his shouting, until a tiny sparrow swallows him whole. The tale in verse is often read as a witty parable about how inflated fear makes a small threat enormous.
fact: Many literary scholars read Chukovsky's tale as political satire on the cult of a dictator's personality.

name: The Chattering Fly
description: A fly in her best clothes who finds a coin on the road and throws a lavish tea party for the woodland guests, until an evil spider attacks. A brave little mosquito comes to her rescue with his sabre drawn. One of the best-loved and most quoted of Chukovsky's tales in verse.
fact: The opening lines about the fly walking through the field and finding a coin can be recited from memory by most Russians.

name: Ellie from "The Wizard of the Emerald City"
description: A girl carried off by a hurricane along with her house into a magical land, where she has to follow a road of yellow brick to find a way home. On the way she gains loyal friends, each of them looking for the thing he lacks. The heroine of a famous Soviet retelling of Frank Baum's book.
fact: Volkov's book is often confused with Frank Baum's original about the American girl Dorothy, though the plots diverged over time.
wiki_en: The Wizard of the Emerald City

name: Totoshka
description: A small but brave little dog, swept into the magical land along with his mistress and never a step behind her on the whole long road. Modest in size as he is, he shows real courage in the face of real danger more than once. The loyal companion of a famous Soviet tale's heroine.
fact: Unlike Frank Baum's Toto, Volkov's Totoshka starts speaking in human words the moment he lands in the Magic Land.
wiki_en: The Wizard of the Emerald City

name: The Scarecrow
description: A scarecrow stuffed with straw and hung on a pole in the middle of a field, who comes to life and joins Ellie in the hope of getting a real brain. For all his doubts about his own mind, he keeps coming up with the cleverest solutions. One of the best-loved characters in the Magic Land tale.
fact: In the course of the story the Scarecrow becomes ruler of the Emerald City, proving he had plenty of wit from the start.
wiki_en: The Wizard of the Emerald City

name: The Iron Woodman
description: Once an ordinary woodcutter, he had every part of his body replaced with iron through witchcraft and lost his heart along with them. He joins Ellie in the hope of being able to feel and to love again, and shows extraordinary kindness to the weak despite having no heart.
fact: What the Iron Woodman fears most in the world is rusting in the rain, so he always carries an oilcan with him.
wiki_en: The Wizard of the Emerald City

name: The Cowardly Lion
description: A mighty-looking king of the forest beasts who in fact is terrified of everything and longs to find real courage. He joins Ellie's journey to the Emerald City along with the Scarecrow and the Iron Woodman, and proves again and again that bravery is acting in spite of fear, not the absence of it.
fact: For all his nickname, the Cowardly Lion saves his friends repeatedly, taking on genuinely dangerous creatures of the Magic Land.
wiki_en: The Wizard of the Emerald City

name: Uncle Fyodor
description: A boy far more self-reliant than his years, who moves out to the village of Prostokvashino with the talking cat Matroskin and the dog Sharik, to his parents' considerable surprise. He runs the household, acquires a cow and copes with the difficult characters of his unusual pets.
fact: The famous cartoon "Three from Prostokvashino", made from this book, came out in 1978 and got two sequels.
wiki_en: Uncle Fyodor, His Dog, and His Cat

name: Sharik the Dog
description: A simple-hearted hunting dog who left the city with Uncle Fyodor and settled in the village of Prostokvashino. He dreams of getting a gun and taking up hunting, and bickers constantly over trifles with the level-headed cat Matroskin. One of Soviet animation's most recognisable voices.
fact: In the cartoon Sharik ends up with a camera instead of a real gun and hunts animals by photographing them.
wiki_en: Uncle Fyodor, His Dog, and His Cat

name: Postman Pechkin
description: A fussy, suspicious village postman who starts out at odds with the new residents of Prostokvashino because the boy has no papers. In time he thaws and becomes a good friend to Uncle Fyodor and his pets. One of the most quoted characters in the Prostokvashino cartoons.
fact: Given a bicycle as a present, Pechkin delivers a famous line: "Why was I so nasty before? Because I had no bicycle."
wiki_en: Uncle Fyodor, His Dog, and His Cat

name: Kuzya the House Spirit
description: A shaggy, good-natured little house spirit who lives behind the stove and keeps order in a village cottage, until he is moved into a modern city flat. Grumbling and superstitious, he takes a while to adjust, but grows sincerely attached to a girl named Natasha.
fact: In the cartoons Kuzya has an older mentor, the ancient house spirit Nafanya, whom he runs to with all his troubles.

name: The Hare from "Nu, Pogodi!"
description: The charming, resourceful hare who is the hapless Wolf's chief target in the famous Soviet cartoon series. Time after time he slips out of the chase by using his wits rather than force. One of the most recognisable and best-loved characters in Soviet animation.
fact: For all that the series is named after the Wolf's threat, it is the Hare who almost always comes out on top.

name: Piglet
description: A tiny, timid pig, Winnie-the-Pooh's best friend, who worries about absolutely everything yet always turns up when his friends need him. Fainthearted as he is, he shows real courage more than once for the sake of those he loves. One of the tenderest characters in A. A. Milne's books.
fact: In the Russian translation he is Pyatachok, "little snout", named after a pig's nose.

name: Eeyore
description: The perpetually gloomy, pessimistic donkey of the Hundred Acre Wood, whose tail keeps trying to fall off. For all his dark forebodings about everything, he sincerely values his friends' attention, especially on his own birthday. Children's literature's best-loved melancholic.
fact: In a well-known chapter the friends have to arrange Eeyore's birthday, and his presents are a burst balloon and an empty honey pot.

name: Rabbit
description: The busy, slightly grumbling resident of the Hundred Acre Wood, proud of his vegetable patch and of the order in his own burrow. He is forever organising things for his friends, though he does not always consider what they actually want. The most practical character in Milne's books.
fact: It is in Rabbit's narrow burrow that Winnie-the-Pooh gets stuck, having eaten too much honey before setting off home.

name: Chiko
description: A level-headed, well-read hedgehog who values quiet philosophical conversation and a good book above noisy adventures. One of the calmest and most sensible characters in the cartoon series, he often serves as the voice of reason among his more impulsive friends.
fact: The hedgehog and the restless rabbit Krash are the show's best-known pair of friends: many episodes are built on the contrast.

name: Rosa
description: A pink, flirtatious little pig devoted to outfits, make-up and everyone's attention, who nonetheless genuinely cares about her friends. Behind the outward vanity is a vulnerable, kind nature. One of the brightest and most recognisable characters in the series.
fact: She is one of the show's two main female characters; the other, the sensible owl Olga, is far older and calmer.

name: Wally
description: A curly-fleeced ram with an artistic soul, given to melancholy, poetry and romantic suffering over anything at all. He often drifts off into his own fantasies, and remains the most lyrical character in the series. His sensitivity is a constant occasion for his friends' gentle teasing.
fact: Wally writes poems all the time, and is almost never satisfied with a single line of them.

name: Barry
description: A good-natured, hard-working bear who devotes every spare hour to his own vegetable patch and orchard. Unhurried, sensible and always ready to share the harvest with his friends. One of the most even-tempered and solidly practical characters in the series.
fact: His Russian name, Kopatych, comes from the verb for digging, which is exactly how he spends his days.

name: Luigi
description: Mario's more timid, more nervous younger twin, also a plumber and also forever dragged into saving the Mushroom Kingdom. He wears green where his brother wears red, and made his name above all hunting ghosts in the haunted mansion games. One of the most recognisable characters in video games.
fact: For the thirtieth anniversary of his first appearance, Nintendo declared 2013 the "Year of Luigi" and gave him several games.

name: Princess Peach
description: The ruler of the Mushroom Kingdom, whose kidnapping by the villain Bowser sets off Mario's adventures over and over again. For all the image of the perpetual victim, in some games she takes up weapons and powers herself and proves a nimble, resourceful character.
fact: In some games in the series Princess Peach can hover briefly in the air, using her dress as a parachute.

name: Bowser
description: The enormous horned king of the Koopa turtles, who kidnaps Princess Peach from game to game and keeps trying to seize the Mushroom Kingdom. He breathes fire, commands an army of minions and has an airborne fleet of his own. One of the longest-lived villains in video games.
fact: Villain as he is, in some games in the series Bowser becomes Mario's temporary ally against even more dangerous enemies.

name: Link
description: A silent young man in a green tunic, called by fate in game after game to save the kingdom of Hyrule from the dark lord Ganon. He wields the legendary Master Sword, an elven bow and a host of other tools for solving intricate puzzles. One of the most enduring heroes in video games.
fact: Link never speaks a line out loud: through almost the entire history of the series he remains a completely mute character.

name: Princess Zelda
description: The wise princess of the kingdom of Hyrule, keeper of the Triforce of Wisdom, whose fate is entwined with Link's story in every game. From one game to the next she appears in different guises, from captive victim to warrior in her own right. One of the oldest female characters in video games.
fact: The whole legendary series is named after Princess Zelda, even though the playable hero is nearly always Link.

name: Master Chief
description: John-117, a super-soldier from the secret Spartan programme, who fights in heavy combat armour against the alien alliance known as the Covenant. Taciturn, disciplined and almost never seen without his helmet. One of the great emblems of the video game industry at the turn of the century.
fact: Master Chief's actual face under the helmet is almost never shown in close-up across most of the series.

name: Duke Nukem
description: A muscle-bound video game hero with slicked-back blond hair, dark glasses and an inexhaustible supply of cocky one-liners. He fights off alien invaders while breaking the fourth wall with parodies of 1980s action films. One of the most recognisable and most cartoonish figures of nineties gaming.
fact: Duke's famous line, "It's time to kick ass and chew bubble gum", is one of the most quoted in video game history.

name: Agent 47
description: A bald professional killer with a trademark barcode on the back of his head, grown in a secret laboratory as the product of genetic experiments. He carries out the Agency's contracts with icy composure, disguising himself expertly as all manner of people. A defining hero of stealth action games.
fact: The number 47 is simply the last digits of the long barcode tattooed on the back of his head.

name: Kratos
description: A former Spartan warrior, tricked into killing his own family and ever since turning his rage on the gods of Olympus. He fights with a pair of chaos blades chained to his arms. One of the most powerful and recognisable heroes the games industry has produced.
fact: The ashes of his dead family fused to Kratos's skin and turned it white, which is why he is called the Ghost of Sparta.

name: Altaïr
description: A master assassin of the late 12th century, active during the Third Crusade and hunting nine powerful Templars in the Holy Land. He carries a hidden blade and the legendary gift of eagle vision. The hero of the first Assassin's Creed and a symbol of the whole franchise.
fact: Altaïr was the series' first hero, and the player relives his memories through the Animus machine, in the eyes of a distant descendant.

name: Ezio Auditore
description: A young Florentine nobleman of the Renaissance who, after a tragedy in his own family, devotes his life to the Order of Assassins and the war on the Templars. He travels from vengeful youth to wise mentor of a new generation of killers. One of the most loved heroes in the series.
fact: Ezio's story stretches across three full games in the series, following him from his youth to his mature years.

name: Arthur Morgan
description: A seasoned member of Dutch van der Linde's gang, riding through an America of 1899 at the very close of the Wild West. He combines a gunman's rough hardness with a private code of honour of his own. One of the most deeply written characters in modern video games.
fact: Arthur Morgan's journal, which the player fills in as the game goes on, was praised as one of gaming's finest ways of revealing a character.

name: Joel
description: A hard-bitten smuggler surviving in an America twenty years after the start of an epidemic that turns people into infected monsters. He takes on escorting a teenage girl across dangerous territory, which forces him to open up to feeling again. One of gaming's most powerful characters.
fact: Joel learned the guitar as a child, and the instrument recurs as an important detail of his story throughout the game.

name: Ellie from "The Last of Us"
description: A fourteen-year-old girl raised in a world after the pandemic, carrying the rarest of things: immunity to the infection. Sharp-tongued and resourceful, she grows up fast under the weight of what she lives through on a long journey across a dangerous country.
fact: The tattoo of a moth and fern leaves she has in the sequel covers the scar of an infected bite.

name: Gordon Freeman
description: A young research physicist at the Black Mesa complex who finds himself, by chance, at the centre of a catastrophe that opens a portal to a world of hostile aliens. He is so taciturn that he never speaks a single line in the entire series. His glasses and crowbar are gaming icons.
fact: By his in-game biography, Gordon Freeman is a doctor of theoretical physics who took his degree at MIT.

name: Sam Fisher
description: A special forces veteran turned covert operative for a secret unit that works outside the law in the name of national security. A master of silent infiltration who uses shadow and high-technology gear, including his unmistakable night vision goggles. A defining hero of stealth action.
fact: The distinctive green three-dot glow of Sam Fisher's night vision goggles became one of the genre's most recognisable images.

name: Solid Snake
description: A legendary operative who infiltrates enemy bases alone to stop the threat of a nuclear walking tank, the Metal Gear. A master of disguise and stealth, able to hide from enemies for hours in the unlikeliest of places. One of the great emblems of stealth action in video games.
fact: Hiding from enemies under an ordinary cardboard box is Solid Snake's signature and surprisingly effective trick.

name: Dante from Devil May Cry
description: Half human, half demon, he inherited inhuman strength from his demon father and became a hunter of other demons for money and for the fun of it. He combines virtuoso swordplay and gunfire with showy, insolent bravado. One of the most stylish heroes of the hack-and-slash genre.
fact: Dante's trademark crimson coat and white hair have been the signature of the character from the very first game.

name: Bayonetta
description: A formidable witch in a tight suit made of her own hair, who fights the forces of heaven with four pistols at once. She combines elegant acrobatics with devastating firepower and an ironic sense of style. One of the most recognisable heroines of the hack-and-slash genre.
fact: Bayonetta carries all four pistols at the same time: two in her hands and two more fixed to her heels.

name: Nathan Drake
description: A charming adventurer and descendant of a famous navigator, chasing legendary treasures and lost cities across the world. He has the wit of a Hollywood adventure hero, an acrobat's agility and a marksman's aim. One of the most recognisable heroes in action-adventure gaming.
fact: The game's creators admitted they took Indiana Jones as their model when they built Nathan Drake's character and adventures.

name: Vegeta
description: The proud prince of the all but exterminated Saiyan race, at first the enemy of the hero Son Goku and in time his chief rival and ally. He is obsessed with becoming the strongest warrior in the universe and never accepts anyone else's superiority.
fact: The former enemy eventually acquires a family on Earth: his wife is Bulma and his son is Trunks.

name: Edward Elric
description: A gifted teenage alchemist who lost an arm and a leg, now replaced by mechanical limbs, after a failed attempt to bring his dead mother back. With his younger brother he sets out to find a way to recover the bodies they lost. A famous hero of manga and anime about the cost of forbidden alchemy.
fact: Young as he is, Edward Elric holds the official rank of State Alchemist of Amestris, a rare honour for a teenager.

name: Ichigo Kurosaki
description: An ordinary high-school student able to see spirits, who accidentally inherits the powers of a Soul Reaper, the guide of the dead into the next world. He starts fighting the dangerous spirits known as Hollows to protect both the living and the dead. A defining hero of 21st-century manga.
fact: Ichigo's bright orange hair is a running joke among the other characters from the very beginning of the story.

name: Sanji
description: The elegant cook of the Straw Hat pirate crew, who fights exclusively with his legs so as to keep his hands safe for cooking. Gallant towards women almost to the point of caricature, he dreams of finding the legendary sea called All Blue. One of the leads of the cult manga and anime.
fact: Sanji makes it a matter of principle never to hit a woman, even when one is fighting him directly.

name: Roronoa Zoro
description: A former bounty hunter who became the first member of the Straw Hat crew and means to be the greatest swordsman in the world. He fights with three swords at once in a unique style, clenching one blade in his teeth. Infamous for his phenomenal talent for getting lost.
fact: For all his reputation as a fearsome fighter, Zoro regularly gets lost inside his own ship, a running joke in the series.

name: Shinji Ikari
description: A fourteen-year-old boy summoned by his distant, demanding father to pilot a giant biomechanical robot, an Evangelion, in defence of Tokyo-3 against the mysterious beings called Angels. He is torn apart by self-doubt and by fear of being rejected by those closest to him.
fact: The psychological depth and ambiguity of Shinji Ikari made the series the subject of endless analysis and argument among viewers.

name: Asuka Langley
description: The ambitious, hot-tempered young pilot of the red Evangelion, raised from childhood as a prodigy and obsessed with having to be the best at everything. Behind the show of self-assurance she hides deep insecurity and a fear of being alone. A defining heroine of nineties anime.
fact: Asuka arrives in Tokyo-3 from Germany, where she was trained as a pilot together with her red Eva-02.

name: Aladdin
description: A quick-witted street pauper in an eastern city who happens on a magic lamp with a wish-granting genie inside. He uses the chance to change his fate to win a princess's heart and to prove that birth does not determine a person's true worth.
fact: The original tale of Aladdin does not come from the Arabic manuscripts: a French translator added it to the collection in the early 18th century.

name: The Genie
description: A mighty spirit imprisoned in a magic lamp and bound to grant three wishes to whoever frees him. He combines all but limitless magical power with centuries of weariness at serving other people's wishes. Popular culture's most recognisable genie, thanks above all to the Disney film.
fact: The rules of his magic forbid him to raise the dead, to make anyone fall in love, or to grant more than the allotted number of wishes.

name: Jasmine
description: The headstrong princess of the eastern sultanate of Agrabah, tired of palace convention and determined to choose her own fate and her own husband. She keeps a tame tiger, Rajah, and is not afraid to slip out of the palace to see how the city really lives.
fact: Jasmine was one of the first Disney princesses to openly rebel against marriage by arrangement rather than by love.

name: Mulan
description: The daughter of a Chinese warrior, who secretly takes her sick father's place in the imperial army by disguising herself as a man. She goes through harsh military training alongside the men and proves her valour and resourcefulness in battle. Based on an ancient Chinese legend.
fact: The real legend of the warrior woman Hua Mulan behind the film has been told in China for more than a thousand years.

name: Pocahontas
description: The freedom-loving daughter of the chief of the Powhatan people, whose meeting with English colonists becomes a test of understanding between two utterly different worlds. She is closely bound to nature and to the wisdom of her ancestors. Based on a real historical figure.
fact: The real Pocahontas was the daughter of Chief Powhatan, and her actual life turned out very differently from the film.

name: Belle
description: A clever, well-read young woman in provincial France who feels a stranger among her neighbours for loving books and dreaming of more. To save her father she agrees to stay as a prisoner in the castle of an enchanted Beast. One of the first Disney princesses to value mind and kindness over looks.
fact: Belle was the first Disney princess whose film was nominated for the Academy Award for best picture.

name: The Beast
description: Once a spoiled young prince, turned into a beast by an enchantress as punishment for his coldness and arrogance. He has to learn to love and be loved before the last petal falls from a magic rose. One of Disney animation's most recognisable images of redemption.
fact: The studio's artists built the Beast's appearance out of features of several animals at once: a lion, a boar, a gorilla and a bear.

name: Gaston
description: A vain village hunter used to getting whatever he wants through strength and charm. He is certain that Belle simply owes it to him to become his wife, and cannot understand her indifference to his person. One of the most vividly cartoonish villains in Disney animation.
fact: Gaston was one of the first Disney villains whose menace rests not on magic but on ordinary human vanity and brute force.

name: Ursula
description: A cunning octopus sea witch, living in exile on the edge of the undersea kingdom and striking ruinous bargains with naive petitioners. She takes the mermaid Ariel's voice in exchange for human legs, with a treacherous plan of her own. One of Disney's most theatrical villains.
fact: Ursula's look and manner owe a great deal to the famous drag performer Divine.

name: Mater
description: A rusty old tow truck from the backwater town of Radiator Springs, guileless and impossibly talkative. He becomes the best friend of the arrogant race car Lightning McQueen and helps him find a place in the little town's community. One of Pixar's most endearing supporting characters.
fact: Mater can drive backwards faster than most other cars can drive forwards.

name: Judy Hopps
description: A determined rabbit from a small farming village who, against everybody's doubts, becomes the first rabbit police officer in the big city of Zootopia. She runs into prejudice and stereotypes about what small, seemingly harmless animals are capable of.
fact: "Zootopia" won the Academy Award for best animated feature, and took more than a billion dollars at the box office.

name: Nick Wilde
description: A charming street fox and swindler who has spent years making a living from petty scams and has resigned himself to the reputation of a sly, untrustworthy predator. A forced partnership with a rabbit police officer makes him rethink his own life and abilities.
fact: Nick Wilde dreamed as a child of belonging to society, and turned to the cynical con-man act only after running into others' prejudice.

name: Anna
description: The cheerful, impetuous younger princess of the kingdom of Arendelle, raised apart from her elder sister Elsa because of Elsa's magic. She sets out on a dangerous journey through snowbound mountains to repair her bond with her sister and save their kingdom.
fact: Anna's streak of white hair appears after she is struck by her own sister's ice magic.

name: Olaf
description: A guileless and impossibly kind snowman brought to life by Princess Elsa's magic, who naively dreams of one day seeing summer. He has no idea that warmth is dangerous to a body made of snow, which is a constant source of comedy. One of the best-loved supporting characters in modern Disney animation.
fact: Olaf genuinely longs to feel the summer sun on his own skin, with no notion of what that would mean for him.

name: Ross Geller
description: A palaeontologist specialising in dinosaurs, whose private life turns into a run of divorces, jealousy and excruciating situations in full view of his friends. One of the six leads of the cult sitcom, and the source of much of its self-destructive humour.
fact: Ross's line "We were on a break!" became one of the most recognisable and most quoted in the show's history.

name: Rachel Green
description: The spoiled daughter of wealthy parents, who runs out on her own wedding and starts life over as a waitress at the Central Perk coffee house. Over the seasons she goes from a helpless follower of fashion to a confident career woman in the fashion industry.
fact: Rachel's haircut, as worn by Jennifer Aniston, became one of the most copied women's hairstyles of the nineties.

name: Chandler Bing
description: A sarcastic office employee with a mysterious job that he himself can never quite explain to his friends. He hides his insecurity behind an almost unbroken stream of irony and self-mocking jokes. One of the six leads of the cult sitcom "Friends".
fact: Even Chandler's own friends in the show admit more than once that they never really worked out what he does at work.

name: Monica Geller
description: A chef obsessed with cleanliness and order, whose demands on herself and everyone else go back to a difficult childhood next to her more favoured brother Ross. She organises the whole group's life, taking on the role of hostess of the flat.
fact: As a teenager, the show's story goes, Monica was much heavier, something the flashbacks return to again and again.

name: Phoebe Buffay
description: An eccentric masseuse and street singer with a hard past and absurdly funny songs of her own writing. She is the free spirit of the group, living by her own rules and believing in the mystical whatever her friends may say about it.
fact: Phoebe's song "Smelly Cat" was performed live on the show by the actress Lisa Kudrow herself.

name: Tony Soprano
description: An Italian-American mafia boss from New Jersey, juggling a brutal criminal trade with the cares of an ordinary suburban family man. He secretly sees a therapist, trying to cope with panic attacks and the weight of his own decisions. The lead of a series that changed television drama.
fact: "The Sopranos" and Tony himself are counted among the main inspirations for the whole later wave of dramas with morally ambiguous leads.

name: Dwight Schrute
description: An eccentric sales manager at a paper company and a farmer on the side, fixated on rules, martial arts and his own ideas about chains of command. His literal, peculiar view of the world is a permanent source of comedy in the office.
fact: Dwight Schrute grows beets on the family farm, a fact he will share with colleagues at practically any opportunity.

name: Jim Halpert
description: A sales manager at a paper company who gets through the boredom of the working day with office pranks, most of them aimed at his colleague Dwight. He turns regularly to the camera with an ironic look at the absurdity going on around him.
fact: One of Jim's favourite pranks is sealing Dwight's stationery in jelly, right there on his desk.

name: Hodor
description: The good-natured, immensely strong servant of House Stark, able to say only his own name in place of any other word. Behind the apparent simplicity is deep devotion to the family he serves faithfully. One of the most moving supporting characters in "A Song of Ice and Fire".
fact: The real reason he can say only one word is revealed many years after his first appearance in the story.

name: Cersei Lannister
description: The ambitious queen from the mighty House Lannister, ready for any intrigue and any sacrifice for power and for her children's safety. Her mind and her composure match, and sometimes surpass, those of the men at court. One of the saga's most ambiguous and memorable figures.
fact: It is Cersei Lannister who speaks the famous line: when you play the game of thrones, you win or you die.

name: Jaime Lannister
description: A brilliant swordsman and knight of the Kingsguard whose reputation is clouded for years by one disputed act in his past. Over the course of the story he travels a long road of rethinking his own honour and his place in the world. One of the saga's most contradictory characters.
fact: The nickname Kingslayer follows Jaime Lannister for years, though the real reasons for what he did stay unknown to those around him for a long time.

name: Arya Stark
description: The headstrong younger daughter of House Stark, who from childhood prefers swordplay to the usual occupations of a noble girl. After terrible losses she goes through a hard schooling in survival and in the craft of a fighter. One of the saga's most resilient and best-loved heroines.
fact: Arya's sword training begins with a tiny blade called Needle, a gift from her older half-brother Jon Snow.

name: Eddard Stark
description: The stern, honest lord of the northern castle of Winterfell, who puts duty and honour above his own advantage and safety. His unbending directness is in sharp contrast with the treachery of the royal court, into which he is drawn. A central figure of the saga's first book.
fact: The Stark words, "Winter is coming", are bound up above all with Eddard Stark and his sense of always being ready for the worst.

name: The Dude
description: An unemployed devotee of bowling and White Russians known as the Dude, whose unhurried way of life is upset by an absurd mix-up with a millionaire of the same name. He meets the most ridiculous events with philosophical calm and minimal effort. The cult hero of the Coen brothers' comedy.
fact: The Dude inspired a whole informal following known as Dudeism, which parodies religious movements in its own laid-back way.

name: Crocodile Dundee
description: A seasoned hunter and tracker from the Australian outback, used to meeting crocodiles and to everything else the bush can throw at him. Dropped into the noise of New York, he calmly applies his survival skills to the troubles of the city. The hero of a cult eighties comedy.
fact: He earned the nickname Crocodile by surviving a fight with one; Dundee is his actual surname.

name: Mary Poppins
description: A stern-looking but extraordinarily kind magical nanny who arrives by umbrella to put the London household of the Banks family in order. She turns dull chores into adventures with small miracles and unshakeable tact. One of the most recognisable figures in English children's literature.
fact: Disney's 1964 film won Julie Andrews an Oscar, though P. L. Travers herself was unhappy with the adaptation.

name: Neville Longbottom
description: At first a clumsy, timid Gryffindor student who is forever losing his things and muddling the simplest spells. As the story goes on he discovers his own talent for herbology and a firmness of character nobody expected of him. One of the series' most touching cases of growing up.
fact: It is Neville Longbottom who pulls the legendary sword of Gryffindor from the Sorting Hat at one of the series' tensest moments.

name: Draco Malfoy
description: An arrogant Slytherin student from a pure-blood wizarding family, Harry Potter's rival from his very first day at Hogwarts. He covers his own insecurity, and the pressure his family puts on him, with snobbery and disdain. One of the series' most ambiguous school antagonists.
fact: Across the seven books, Draco Malfoy's relationship with Harry Potter becomes a great deal more than simple schoolboy rivalry.
